questions.stem: What is the reason a shadow is formed?
choices: Light is reflected by an object
Light is absorbed by an object
Light is blocked by an object
Light is scattered by an object
questions.solution: Light is blocked by an object, which prevents it from reaching a surface, creating a shadow. Reflection occurs when light bounces off a surface, absorption occurs when light is taken in by a material, and scattering happens when light spreads out in different directions. None of these directly cause a shadow to form.

questions.stem: A student looks at their image in a plane mirror. They raise their left hand, and the image raises its right hand. What is this phenomenon called?
questions.solution: Lateral inversion occurs when the left and right sides of an object are reversed in a mirror image, which is why raising the left hand makes the image appear to raise the right hand. Reflection refers to the general phenomenon of light bouncing off a surface, but it does not specifically describe the left-right reversal. Refraction is the bending of light as it passes through different mediums, and diffusion is the scattering of light in many directions, neither of which explain the mirror's effect.

questions.stem: A person stands 2 meters away from a plane mirror. If they move 1 meter closer to the mirror, what happens to the distance between the person and their image?
